cast.rolePolicy: Scene context establishes the role. Each person can be a consultant, client, colleague or leader; age, gender and ethnicity do not impose a permanent job or hierarchy.
cast.agePolicy: Apparent age is a loose casting direction, not a quota. The user prioritizes characters that visually belong together and feel relatable over making executives look very old.
cast.pairingIntent: When Ravi and Helen appear together, they should read as experienced colleagues in the same professional generation. Use their current faces as the age/maturity references; exact numerical ages are secondary.

styleRules: Keep smooth vector-like curves, deliberate dark outlines and two or three intentional shades per material.
Keep each person's approved face, age, complexion, hair, build, garment shape and accessories consistent with their individual masters; take fabric colors from the approved wardrobe reference.
Use shared colors selectively for props and accents. Preserve each character's final distinct wardrobe palette rather than dressing the cast in an aqua or mint uniform.
Preserve natural differences in skin and hair; do not apply Nia's complexion to the whole cast.
Use transparent backgrounds and small intentional ground shadows. Avoid cream paper, yellow or sepia washes, room backdrops, grain and glow halos.
Keep text, labels, logos and business claims outside the image where possible.
Use new actions and meaningful props for new scenes. The master reference pose and notebook are not required in every scene.
Attach an identity reference for each selected character. Additional people shown in style-only references must not appear unless requested.
Preserve existing illustrations. Save each new scene or identity revision under a new versioned filename.
Review a changed identity before using it as an approved reference. The current consulting illustration refresh is reviewed one image at a time.
Final website illustrations must use native SVG paths and shapes, without embedded or linked bitmaps or foreignObject content.

stylePriority: Visual cohesion with the established cast and reader identification take priority over making characters visibly old, highly formal or anatomically realistic. Review each revision beside the rest of the cast.
